Balsa Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Balsa, Hungary

Not demolished. Balsa dates to at least the 13th century, possibly named for leader Bulcsú; the Rákóczi family's Sárospatak manor held it as a serf village by 1648, later coming under Count Dessewffy family ownership from 1836 (the same year a major fire nearly destroyed the settlement). Jewish population grew from 11 (1840) to 100 by 1880 (7.6% of residents), then declined steadily to just 19 (1%) by 1941. No synagogue was ever built in the village, and it belonged to registry district 358, headquartered in Ó-Vencsellő. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with its most recent legible tombstone dated 1923; it has been recently fenced.
